# Greenville Fishing

> Taylor LeBlanc is a fishing guide based in Greenville, South Carolina, guiding through Mt. Yonder Fly Fishing (https://mtyonder.com). He specializes in trophy largemouth bass on small water, fall and winter smallmouth on the rivers of Western North Carolina, summer creek bass, and beginner lessons, mostly on foot, fly rod or conventional. Trips book through Mt. Yonder by phone at 864.816.0506; ask for Taylor. Half day $300, full day $385 for one angler, prices set by Mt. Yonder, verified 2026-09-10. Newsletter: The Water Report, https://greenvillefishing.beehiiv.com.

- [Where I guide](https://greenvillefishing.com/where-i-guide/): Where a Greenville fishing guide fishes: the Reedy downtown, foothill creeks inside 30 minutes, small trophy lakes inside 45, the French Broad in fall.
- [What I fish for, by season](https://greenvillefishing.com/seasons/): What a Greenville guide targets by month: pre-spawn largemouth in February, bluegill-bed bass in summer, trophy smallmouth in October and November.

- [Questions people ask before a trip](https://greenvillefishing.com/faq/): Do you need to know how to fish, fly or spin, can kids come, what to wear, what Taylor brings, what happens when it rains, and the honest odds of a giant.
- [Gallery](https://greenvillefishing.com/gallery/): Trophy largemouth, fall smallmouth, creek bass and carp from guided days near Greenville, SC, with the numbers. Every fish went back.

- [Blog](https://greenvillefishing.com/blog/): Longer pieces on bass fishing around Greenville, SC and the rivers of Western North Carolina: seasons, patterns, tackle, and how I fish for them.

## Blog
- [Where to Fish Near Greenville, SC](https://greenvillefishing.com/blog/where-to-fish-near-greenville-sc/), September 12, 2026: Public water near Greenville, SC that anyone can fish, by drive time from downtown: the Reedy, the Saluda, park lakes, trout streams and the reservoirs.
- [Sight-Fishing for Largemouth Bass: What to Expect on a Spring Trip](https://greenvillefishing.com/blog/spring-sight-fishing-largemouth/), September 11, 2026: How largemouth behave from pre-spawn through the bluegill beds, and how a bank angler targets each stage for the biggest bass of the year.
- [The Reedy River in Downtown Greenville](https://greenvillefishing.com/blog/reedy-river-downtown-greenville/), September 11, 2026: A small river in the heart of downtown Greenville: big redbreast sunfish, largemouth bass and a few big ones, fishable from the Swamp Rabbit Trail.
- [Targeting Giant Smallmouth in the Fall](https://greenvillefishing.com/blog/fall-smallmouth/), September 11, 2026: After the equinox, smallmouth feed hard and group into compact wintering water. How I find that water and fish it, jerkbaits to dead-sticking.

## Trips (prices set by Mt. Yonder Fly Fishing, verified 2026-09-10)
- Trophy Largemouth: The flagship. Sight fishing on foot for one class of fish, on small clear water most Greenville anglers drive past. Fewer bites, bigger ones, and you make the casts while I coach. Half day $300 (one angler) or $400 (two); full day $385 or $500, lunch included on full days.
- Fall and Winter Trophy Smallmouth: The cold-water trophy window. October and November are the best two months of the year for a big smallmouth here, and they are the two nobody books. Winter runs it deeper and slower. Half day $300 (one angler) or $400 (two); full day $385 or $500, lunch included on full days.
- Summer Creek Smallmouth and Bartram's Bass: The niche trip. Wet wading a foothill creek with one rod and a small box, for smallmouth and the Bartram's bass, a fish a few outfitters sell trips for and most anglers have never held. Poppers and topwater in warm water. Half day $300 (one angler) or $400 (two); full day $385 or $500, lunch included on full days.
- Beginners Bank Bass Fishing Lessons: The low-barrier entry, for people who think they are not a fishing person. Tackle supplied, patience included, success measured in bent rods and confidence. Kids and teens do well here. Half day $300 (one angler) or $400 (two); full day $385 or $500, lunch included on full days.

## Booking
- Call Mt. Yonder Fly Fishing at 864.816.0506 and ask for Taylor.
- Or book the walk and wade trip online at https://mtyonder.com/products/classic-guided-walk-and-wade-fly-fishing-trip and put Taylor and the trip name in the order note.

## Notes
- Taylor never names the specific water he fishes. Regions, rivers and public parks are described; honey holes are not.
- Every fish is released.
- No trip guarantees a particular fish; the site describes patterns, not promises.
- Reviews quoted on the site are verbatim from Mt. Yonder Fly Fishing's Google profile and from Instagram, attributed by first name.
